policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV lists only "the chief priests, and the elders of the people"; no "and the scribes" answering the added καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς.

Pure Greek word order (ἔχουσα before or after ἀλάβαστρον μύρου); ASV "a woman having an alabaster cruse" renders either identically. The two notes are alternative_rendering and do not bear on the reading.
Genitive τῆς κεφαλῆς vs accusative τὴν κεφαλὴν after ἐπί; both yield ASV "upon his head" with no English difference.
ASV reads "the disciples", not "his disciples"; no possessive answering the added αὐτοῦ.
ASV reads "this ointment" with the noun unitalicized, i.e. represented in the Greek; the base τοῦτο alone would give a bare "this".
ASV has "the disciples came to Jesus, saying" — the participle is rendered and there is no "unto him" answering αὐτῷ.
Aorist subjunctive vs future indicative of ἑτοιμάζω in a deliberative clause; ASV "that we make ready" renders either.
ASV text reads "the twelve disciples", and its mapped textual_variant note "Many authorities, some ancient, omit disciples" places the omission in the margin, so the text carries μαθητῶν.
ASV "began to say unto him every one" has no "of them" answering αὐτῶν in ἕκαστος αὐτῶν.
Word order of τὴν χεῖρα and ἐν τῷ τρυβλίῳ only; ASV "dipped his hand with me in the dish" follows English order and distinguishes neither. The lone note is a cross-reference.
Presence or absence of the article with ἄρτον; ASV "took bread" leaves a Greek article untranslated either way.
ASV renders "blessed" here and "gave thanks" at v.27 for εὐχαριστήσας, so the verb here is εὐλογήσας.
Participle δοὺς vs imperfect ἐδίδου with added καί; ASV routinely renders a circumstantial aorist participle as a coordinated finite verb, so "and he gave to the disciples, and said" fits either.
ASV text reads "a cup" and its mapped textual_variant note "Some ancient authorities read the cup" assigns the article to the margin.
An added article τὸ in the attributive chain after μου; no English exponent either way. The verse note concerns "new" (καινῆς), a different unit.
ASV text reads "my blood of the covenant" and its mapped textual_variant note "Many ancient authorities insert new" puts καινῆς in the margin.
Added recitative ὅτι after ὑμῖν; ASV "But I say unto you, I shall not drink" leaves such a ὅτι untranslated, so nothing distinguishes it.
Plural vs singular verb with the neuter plural subject τὰ πρόβατα; ASV "the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad" cannot show Greek verb number.
Added connective δὲ with ἐγὼ; ASV's "But" renders the preceding ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ, and "I will never be offended" carries no further connective, which ASV would in any case be free to leave untranslated.
Future indicative vs aorist subjunctive after οὐ μή; ASV "yet will I not deny thee" renders either construction the same.
Added δὲ after ὁμοίως; ASV "Likewise also said all the disciples" — "also" answers καί, and an added δὲ would leave no separate trace.
Word order of ἐκεῖ and προσεύξωμαι only; ASV "while I go yonder and pray" distinguishes neither. The note is a Greek gloss on Γεθσημανή.
ASV reads "Then saith he unto them"; the pronoun subject shows no explicit ὁ Ἰησοῦς in the text.
ASV "he went forward a little" renders προελθών; προσελθών would give "came"/"drew near".
ASV "if this cannot pass away" has no "cup" answering τὸ ποτήριον.
ASV "if this cannot pass away, except I drink it" has no "from me" answering ἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ.
ASV renders the aorist εὗρεν as past "found"; this chapter keeps historic presents as presents ("cometh", "saith"), so εὑρίσκει is excluded.
Word order of πάλιν and ἀπελθὼν only; ASV "And he left them again, and went away" fits either arrangement.
ASV has a second "again" in "saying again the same words", answering the πάλιν with εἰπών that the alternative omits.
ASV reads "cometh he to the disciples", not "his disciples"; no possessive answering αὐτοῦ.
Presence or absence of the article τὸ; ASV "Sleep on now, and take your rest" shows no English exponent for it, and the notes here are an alternative rendering and a cross-reference.
Relative ὃ vs ᾧ after ἐφ᾽; ASV's "do that for which thou art come" supplies the imperative and reads the clause as a relative, which either case form permits.
Position of σου relative to τὴν μάχαιραν; ASV "thy sword" renders both orders alike.
ASV "shall perish with the sword" renders ἀπολοῦνται; ἀποθανοῦνται would give "shall die".
ASV has no "now" with "that I cannot beseech my Father"; its single "even now" stands in the following clause with the sending.
ASV "he shall even now send me more than twelve legions" renders ἄρτι in this clause, which the alternative πλείους ἢ lacks.
ASV "I sat daily in the temple teaching" has no "with you" answering πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
Word order of ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ against ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων only; ASV "I sat daily in the temple teaching" contains the same elements either way.
ASV names only "the chief priests and the whole council"; no "and the elders" answering οἱ πρεσβύτεροι καί.
Word order of the pronoun and subjunctive vs future after ὅπως; ASV "that they might put him to death" renders all three alike.
ASV "But afterward came two," lacks the ψευδομάρτυρες and the extra οὐχ εὗρον of r02, excluding it; r00-base and r01 differ only in punctuation and spacing and leave no English trace.
Added object αὐτόν with οἰκοδομῆσαι; ASV's "to build it" supplies a pronoun English requires with either reading. The note is an alternative rendering of ναός.
ASV "And the high priest said unto him" has no "answered" answering ἀποκριθείς.
Added recitative ὅτι before direct speech; ASV "saying, He hath spoken blasphemy" leaves such a ὅτι untranslated.
ASV "ye have heard the blasphemy", not "his blasphemy"; no possessive answering αὐτοῦ.
Word order of ἐκάθητο and ἔξω only; ASV "was sitting without in the court" fits either.
ASV "he denied before them all" has "them" answering αὐτῶν; the base ἔμπροσθεν πάντων would give "before all".
Added αὐτὸν as subject of the participle ἐξελθόντα; ASV's "when he was gone out" supplies a subject pronoun English requires either way, and the "him" later is the object of "saw".
ASV "saith unto them that were there" renders the substantival τοῖς ἐκεῖ; αὐτοῖς ἐκεῖ would give simply "unto them there".
ASV "This man also was with Jesus of Nazareth" has "also" answering the initial καί.
εὐθέως and εὐθὺς are the same adverb in two forms; ASV "And straightway the cock crew" cannot distinguish them.
Added article τοῦ with the following name; ASV "the word which Jesus had said" shows no exponent for it.
ASV "the word which Jesus had said" has no "unto him" answering the added αὐτῷ.
